site.name: Android Workbook
site.tagline: Learn the course. See what it builds.
site.intro: A working record of the Android Mobile Application Development (Level-4) course, shared so the next learner has something concrete to study: the modules, the assessment preparation, and several complete implementations of every practical job to compare side by side.

course.title: Android Mobile Application Development
assessedBy: Three timed practical jobs (1 h, 1 h, 2 h)
Written assessment: multiple choice and short answers

modules.title: Working with OOP and Designing Pattern
outcomes: Describe class properties, constants and visibility

modules.title: Working with Android Basic
outcomes: Install and set up the Android development environment

modules.title: Implementing Background Service and Application Deployment

assessment.title: Solved Assessment Bank
assessment.summary: The three practical jobs with working procedure and tools list, plus 37 solved multiple-choice questions, 14 short-answer questions and 10 oral questions.

assessment.title: Oral Preparation
assessment.summary: Module-wise oral questions. Every question has a simple answer, a Bangla answer and a real-life example.

assessment.title: Job 1 Specification Sheet
assessment.summary: REST client: ProductActivity, RecyclerView rows, Retrofit, image loading, connectivity handling and retry.

assessment.title: Job 2 Specification Sheet
assessment.summary: User profile registration with a local SQLite database, full CRUD and MVVM.

assessment.title: Job 3 Specification Sheet
assessment.summary: Location sharing with Firebase Authentication, Cloud Firestore and Google Maps markers.

jobs.title: Product Listing
jobs.subtitle: Consume a REST API
jobs.summary: Download a product list from a public REST API and show it in a scrolling list with images, with loading, error and retry states.
requirements: Parse the JSON and bind it to RecyclerView rows
run: Open one variant folder in Android Studio and let Gradle sync.
Run on an emulator or a device with internet access.
To see the error state, turn on airplane mode, relaunch, then turn it off and tap Retry.

variants.label: Packaged
variants.title: Separated network layer
variants.summary: The API client lives in its own package, away from the screen. The cleanest of the two to read and extend.
highlights: ApiService and RetrofitInstance are separate from ProductActivity
Product and Category models in their own package
Progress bar, error panel and a working Retry button
variants.readIf: you want to see how to keep networking out of the Activity.

variants.label: Compact
variants.title: Assessment-ready, minimal files
variants.summary: Follows the specification naming exactly (name_id_rest01) with the fewest files. Built to be reproduced inside the one-hour limit.
highlights: Four Kotlin files in one package
Retrofit enqueue callback with success and failure paths
Loading, error and Retry handled in a few small functions
variants.readIf: you need the quickest path that still satisfies every line of the spec.

jobs.title: User Profile Registration
jobs.subtitle: Local database and CRUD
jobs.summary: A local profile manager: welcome screen, profile list, add, view, update and delete. Data stays on the device in SQLite, organised with MVVM.
requirements: AddProfileActivity: name, email, date of birth, district, mobile
run: Open one variant folder in Android Studio and let Gradle sync.
Run on an emulator or device (no internet needed).
Add a profile, open it from the list, then try edit and delete.

variants.label: Room
variants.title: Room on top of SQLite
variants.summary: Uses the Room persistence library, which generates the SQLite code for you. The modern, recommended approach.
highlights: DAO with insert, update, delete and query methods
Database singleton
Activities observe LiveData from the ViewModel
variants.readIf: you want the standard Jetpack way to persist data.

variants.label: SQLiteOpenHelper
variants.title: Plain SQLite with no extra libraries
variants.summary: Writes the SQL by hand with SQLiteOpenHelper, ContentValues and cursors, then wraps it in a Repository and ViewModel.
highlights: DatabaseHelper creates the table and implements add, read all, update and delete
No Room dependency, only AndroidX and Material
Shows exactly what Room generates behind the scenes
variants.readIf: the spec says SQLite literally, or you want to understand what Room hides.

jobs.title: Location Sharing
jobs.subtitle: Firebase, Firestore and Maps
jobs.summary: Users register and log in, their location is saved to Cloud Firestore, and everyone appears in a list and as markers on Google Maps.
requirements: Google Map with a marker for every user
run: Complete the setup below (your own Firebase config and Maps key).
Open one variant folder in Android Studio and let Gradle sync.
Run on a device or an emulator with Google Play services.
Register two accounts to see more than one marker.
jobs.setup: This job needs two private values that are intentionally not in the repository: your own google-services.json in the app folder (copy google-services.json.example as a guide) and a line MAPS_API_KEY=your_key in local.properties. Both are git-ignored.

variants.label: MVVM packages
variants.title: Model, repository, viewmodel, ui
variants.summary: A classic MVVM layout with one package per responsibility and a real-time snapshot listener for the friend list.
highlights: UserRepository wraps all Auth and Firestore calls
Four ViewModels: auth, friend list, map, profile
Location updates saved to Firestore
variants.readIf: you want the textbook MVVM structure.

variants.label: Flat
variants.title: Everything in one package
variants.summary: The simplest structure to type under time pressure. Registration is a separate screen, and the Firestore rules are included.
highlights: Auth, register, friend list, map and profile activities side by side
Requests location permission, then saves the user
firestore.rules allows signed-in users only
variants.readIf: you are racing the clock and want the fewest moving parts.

variants.label: View layer
variants.title: model, repository, view, viewmodel
variants.summary: MVVM with an explicit view package, a launcher MainActivity and a live Firestore listener behind the friend list.
highlights: MainActivity routes to AuthActivity
Map marker title is the email, snippet is the display name
Latest Android Studio template and Gradle version catalog
variants.readIf: you prefer naming the UI layer view and want a live-updating list.

variants.label: Styled
variants.title: Polished UI with coroutines
variants.summary: The most complete build: a styled interface, coroutine-based location lookup and a Resource wrapper for loading, success and error states.
highlights: LocationHelper exposes suspend functions for the current and last known location
Resource.Loading, Success and Error drive the screens
Custom drawables for gradient backgrounds, buttons, chips and input fields
variants.readIf: you want a presentation-quality UI and modern async patterns.

skills.detail: Activities, layouts, intents and RecyclerView adapters in every job
Retrofit with a Gson converter, loading, error and retry states
Glide for remote images with caching
Room and plain SQLite with full create, read, update and delete
Repository, ViewModel and LiveData, implemented in four different layouts
Email and password authentication and Cloud Firestore storage
Google Maps SDK markers and the Fused Location Provider
Suspend functions and a Resource state wrapper
API keys kept out of source control using local.properties and Gradle manifest placeholders
